App details

Ham Tools / Radio RF Toolkit

Radio tools for wavelength, power, signal calculations, locators and Morse practice.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

A practical offline toolkit for radio enthusiasts. Work with wavelength, power, antenna matching and signal paths using your own parameters. Convert coordinates to Maidenhead locators, calculate distance and bearing between stations, and practise Morse.

Main features

  • Frequency, wavelength and cable velocity factor.
  • Power, antenna mismatch and entered cable losses.
  • Maidenhead locators, distance and bearing.
  • Morse conversion, playback and practice.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Radio calculations, locations and Morse practice

Wavelength and velocity factor

Enter frequency to get free-space wavelength, half, quarter, five-eighths or your own multiplier. Enter a velocity factor between zero and one, above zero, for reduced propagation length in a cable. These lengths are calculation references, not an automatically corrected final antenna cutting length.

Power, gain/loss and radiated power

Convert watts to dBm/dBW and back, or add a chain of dB gains and losses. Enter transmitter power, feedline loss and antenna gain for ERP/EIRP radiated-power estimates, with dBd or dBi reference explicit. In a resistive RF model, supplied resistance and voltage/current relate to power; regulatory compliance is not decided.

Matching and reflected power

Enter one supported matching value to see SWR, reflection coefficient, return loss, reflected percentage and mismatch loss together. Or enter forward and reflected power to calculate them. Reflected power must stay below positive forward power. These figures help compare matching without inventing antenna properties.

Coaxial-cable loss

Enter cable length and your loss figure for the chosen frequency, in dB per 100 m or 100 ft. See total loss; optional input power gives output power. The result can feed the ERP/EIRP calculation. No hidden manufacturer curve or automatic frequency interpolation supplies missing cable data.

Free-space loss, link budget and Fresnel zone

Frequency and distance give free-space path loss. Add transmitter/receiver gains, cable and explicit extra losses for estimated received power. The first Fresnel-zone calculator shows its radius, midpoint/maximum view and 60% clearance. These help assess an assumed radio link; terrain, buildings and fading are not silently modelled or guaranteed.

Maidenhead, distance and bearing

Convert coordinates to a 4/6/8-character Maidenhead locator or a locator to its cell-centre coordinates. Enter two coordinates or locators to get great-circle distance in km/miles and initial bearing, with reverse bearing where offered. A locator centre is not your exact position. Optional maps may need internet; calculations work without a map.

Morse conversion, reference and playback

Enter supported text for dots and dashes, or typed Morse for text. Look up characters in the reference table. Play the code with your chosen words-per-minute speed and tone frequency; unsupported characters are identified. This is typed conversion and local playback, not automatic decoding of radio audio.

Morse practice

Practise hearing a character or entering/recognising Morse for a character, with random letters, numbers and supported radio punctuation. Limit the character set gradually, adjust speed/tone and view the session’s correct/incorrect results and percentage. This helps a short practice session without keeping a long-term learner profile.

Just one more antenna

Tap the About logo seven times: antennas appear one by one until a roof becomes comically crowded. The offline scene is not an antenna wiring diagram and changes no radio calculation or location data.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
